testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: For a belt-driven air compressor, the belt should be checked to make sure it is:
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each trip. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: The ____ turn on when you press the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Brake lights turn on when you press the brake pedal. Air pressure triggers an electric switch that activates the brake lights.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle, the maximum air leak during an applied leakage test is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi of air pressure per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: If spring brakes are used on a heavy load, stopping will:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. If they activate due to low air pressure, you will need much more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the brake system, it means:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve opens when air pressure gets too high. If this happens, there is a problem in the system that needs to be fixed by a mechanic.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects the air tanks and brake system from too much pressure. It is set to open at 150 psi.

questions.question: Do not drive if a brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before your trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: The ____ between the air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from leaking if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It keeps air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: If only one axle has ABS, what happens?

options.text: You still have more control when braking.
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You still have more control when braking.
questions.explanation: If ABS is on only one axle, the tractor, or the trailer, you will still have more braking control than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.explanation: Air brake vehicles must have a low pressure warning device. A wig wag is one type. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: If brakes create too much heat, what can happen?

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes can fade and stop working if they get too hot. Do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. Also use engine braking.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, what is the maximum air leakage rate in one minute during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle must not lose more than 4 psi of air pressure in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: When should a low air pressure warning signal turn on?

options.text: When tank pressure falls below 120 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 60 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure falls below 60 psi.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning must activate when tank pressure drops below 60 psi. The warning may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: During an emergency stop, what should you do?

options.text: Veer your trailer to the right and stop.
Veer your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a straight line. Use controlled braking or stab braking to keep your vehicle straight and able to turn if needed.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
One air brake system with two different sets of controls.
One system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share one set of controls but each has its own tanks, hoses, and lines. One usually operates the front brakes and one operates the rear brakes.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator stops ice from building up in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is broken?
questions.explanation: A yellow warning light tells the driver that the ABS is not working.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.explanation: Do not push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The springs and air pressure together could damage the brakes.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, what is the safe maximum air leakage during a test?
questions.explanation: The air should not leak more than 3 psi in one minute. If it does, the brakes need to be fixed before you drive.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one may not harm the other.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that builds up in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that builds up in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air has moisture and oil that collect in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks regularly to remove these buildups. Drain them at the end of each driving day.
